title: Biotech news from around the world - Nature Biotechnology
text:
Download PDF

1. UNITED KINGDOMGSK plans to shut its UK R&D headquarters in Stevenage by 2029 and move its operations to a new, 300,000-square-foot site on the Cambridge Biomedical Campus. The company cited direct access to the world-class biomedical research conducted at the University of Cambridge and the surrounding science parks, as well as fully integrated drug development and commercial manufacturing scale-up capability, as reasons for the move. GSK said it will invest $540 million to support the new facility.2. SOUTH KOREASamsung Biologics will buy Swiss contract development and manufacturing organization PolyPeptide Group to boost its peptide, antibody and antibody–drug conjugate production, driven by the demand for obesity treatments and the expansion of peptide-based therapies into new disease areas. The $1.8-billion price tag will be the largest ever purchase by a Korean biopharma company.3. SOUTH AFRICACape Town–based biotech Afrigen secures good manufacturing practice (GMP) certification for its facility, which becomes the continent’s first end-to-end mRNA production site for African vaccine manufacturing. Afrigen has seven vaccine candidates at various stages of development, including vaccines for the Bundibugyo Ebola strain and Rift Valley fever, for which no vaccines currently exist. The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted deep inequality in vaccine access, with the United States and European Union having enough vaccines to cover their populations twice over while the African Union could only cover 38% of the continent’s population. In addition, South Africa’s government paid $5.35 per COVID-19 shot against the EU’s $2.15.4. GUATEMALAGuatemala’s government joins a program that subsidizes climate-resilient, biofortified corn seeds for subsistence farmers. The program, started in 2024 by nonprofit Semilla Nueva, breeds new corn hybrids with the desired traits, provides the parent seeds for new strains for free to partner seed companies, and subsidizes them so they can produce and sell the seed at affordable prices. The government’s $1 million covers 90% of this year’s total subsidies, which will benefit 100,000 farmers.
